claim: Dicer mRNA expression is highest in the hypothalamus of mice at embryonic day (E) 14 and 16.
source: The highest levels of Dicer mRNA were found in hypothalamus of mice at embryonic day (E) 14 and 16, supporting a role for miRNAs in embryonic hypothalamic development (Figure 1a).
evidence: Supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 1a comparing Dicer mRNA levels across developmental stages.

claim: Dicer mRNA levels decrease at postnatal day (P) 10 in the hypothalamus.
source: Dicer mRNA levels decreased at postnatal day (P) 10 and the lowest levels of Dicer mRNA were found in the hypothalamus of adult mice (Figure 1a).
evidence: Supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 1a.

claim: The lowest levels of Dicer mRNA are found in the hypothalamus of adult mice.
source: Dicer mRNA levels decreased at postnatal day (P) 10 and the lowest levels of Dicer mRNA were found in the hypothalamus of adult mice (Figure 1a).
evidence: Supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 1a.

claim: Dicer mRNA is expressed in isolated POMC neurons as early as E13-E15.
source: We next assessed Dicer mRNA expression specifically in POMC neurons and found that Dicer mRNA was expressed in isolated POMC neurons as early as at E13-E15, that is when Pomc progenitor cells differentiate to either POMC or NPY neurons (Figure 1b).
evidence: Supported by RT-qPCR data from sorted POMC neurons shown in Figure 1b.

claim: E13-E15 is when Pomc progenitor cells differentiate to either POMC or NPY neurons.
source: We next assessed Dicer mRNA expression specifically in POMC neurons and found that Dicer mRNA was expressed in isolated POMC neurons as early as at E13-E15, that is when Pomc progenitor cells differentiate to either POMC or NPY neurons (Figure 1b).
evidence: Based on established knowledge about POMC neuron development cited in the manuscript.

claim: Dicer mRNA is highly expressed in NPY neurons at E15.
source: Notably, Dicer mRNA was also highly expressed in NPY neurons at E15 (Figure 1b).
evidence: Supported by RT-qPCR data from sorted NPY neurons shown in Figure 1b.

claim: Pomc-Cre; DicerloxP/loxP male mice display significantly higher body weights compared with control DicerloxP/loxP mice starting at 6 weeks of age.
source: The resulting Pomc-Cre; DicerloxP/loxP male mice displayed significantly higher body weights compared with control DicerloxP/loxP mice starting at 6 weeks of age (Figure 1c and d).
evidence: Supported by body weight measurements shown in Figure 1c and d.

claim: Pomc-Cre; DicerloxP/loxP male mice display reduced oxygen consumption (VO2).
source: In addition, Pomc-Cre; DicerloxP/loxP male mice displayed reduced oxygen consumption (VO2), carbon dioxide production (VCO2), respiratory quotient, energy expenditure, and locomotor activity (Figure 1e–g).
evidence: Supported by indirect calorimetry measurements shown in Figure 1e-g.

claim: Pomc-Cre; DicerloxP/loxP male mice display reduced carbon dioxide production (VCO2).
source: In addition, Pomc-Cre; DicerloxP/loxP male mice displayed reduced oxygen consumption (VO2), carbon dioxide production (VCO2), respiratory quotient, energy expenditure, and locomotor activity (Figure 1e–g).
evidence: Supported by indirect calorimetry measurements shown in Figure 1e-g.

claim: Pomc-Cre; DicerloxP/loxP male mice display reduced respiratory quotient.
source: In addition, Pomc-Cre; DicerloxP/loxP male mice displayed reduced oxygen consumption (VO2), carbon dioxide production (VCO2), respiratory quotient, energy expenditure, and locomotor activity (Figure 1e–g).
evidence: Supported by indirect calorimetry measurements shown in Figure 1e-g.

claim: Pomc-Cre; DicerloxP/loxP male mice display reduced energy expenditure.
source: In addition, Pomc-Cre; DicerloxP/loxP male mice displayed reduced oxygen consumption (VO2), carbon dioxide production (VCO2), respiratory quotient, energy expenditure, and locomotor activity (Figure 1e–g).
evidence: Supported by indirect calorimetry measurements shown in Figure 1e-g.

claim: Pomc-Cre; DicerloxP/loxP male mice display reduced locomotor activity.
source: In addition, Pomc-Cre; DicerloxP/loxP male mice displayed reduced oxygen consumption (VO2), carbon dioxide production (VCO2), respiratory quotient, energy expenditure, and locomotor activity (Figure 1e–g).
evidence: Supported by locomotor activity measurements shown in Figure 1e-g.

claim: Mutant male mice have higher food consumption during dark phase.
source: In addition, mutant male mice had higher food consumption during dark phase (Figure 1h).
evidence: Supported by food intake measurements shown in Figure 1h.

claim: Epididymal fat pad weights are significantly higher in adult Pomc-Cre; DicerloxP/loxP male mice compared with DicerloxP/loxP mice.
source: Epididymal fat pad weights were also significantly higher in adult Pomc-Cre; DicerloxP/loxP male mice compared with DicerloxP/loxP mice (Figure 1i).
evidence: Supported by fat pad weight measurements shown in Figure 1i.

claim: Serum leptin levels are significantly elevated in mutant male mice compared with control mice.
source: Serum leptin levels were also significantly elevated in mutant male mice compared with control mice (Figure 1j).
evidence: Supported by leptin ELISA measurements shown in Figure 1j.

claim: The weight loss effect of leptin is attenuated in Pomc-Cre; DicerloxP/loxP male mice compared with DicerloxP/loxP mice.
source: In addition, we performed leptin sensitivity tests and observed that the weight loss effect of leptin was attenuated in Pomc-Cre; DicerloxP/loxP male mice compared with DicerloxP/loxP mice (Figure 1k).
evidence: Supported by leptin sensitivity test data shown in Figure 1k.

claim: Mutant male mice display impaired glucose tolerance compared with control mice when exposed to a glucose challenge.
source: In addition, when exposed to a glucose challenge, mutant male mice displayed impaired glucose tolerance compared with control mice (Figure 1l).
evidence: Supported by glucose tolerance test data shown in Figure 1l.

claim: Basal insulin levels remain unchanged in mutant male mice.
source: However, basal insulin levels remained unchanged (Figure 1m).
evidence: Supported by insulin ELISA measurements shown in Figure 1m.

claim: Most of the metabolic abnormalities found in male mice are also found in female mice, including increased body weight, food intake, fat mass and reduced VO2, VCO2, and energy expenditure.
source: Most of the metabolic abnormalities were also found in female mice, including increased body weight, food intake, fat mass and reduced VO2, VCO2, and energy expenditure (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Supported by metabolic measurements in female mice shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Adult female mutant mice display impaired glucose tolerance compared with control mice.
source: Adult female mutant mice also displayed impaired glucose tolerance compared with control mice (Figure 1—figure supplement 1f).
evidence: Supported by glucose tolerance test data in female mice shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1f.

claim: Loss of Dicer in POMC neurons has functional consequences on energy balance and glucose regulation.
source: Together, these data indicate that the loss of Dicer in POMC neurons has functional consequences on energy balance and glucose regulation.
evidence: Inferred from the collection of metabolic phenotypes observed in Pomc-Cre; DicerloxP/loxP mice.

claim: POMC neurons in the ARH are generated primarily on embryonic day (E) 11-E12.
source: POMC neurons in the ARH are generated primarily on embryonic day (E) 11-E12 and acquire their terminal peptidergic phenotype during mid-late gestation (Padilla et al., 2010).
evidence: Supported by citation to Padilla et al., 2010.

claim: POMC neurons acquire their terminal peptidergic phenotype during mid-late gestation.
source: POMC neurons in the ARH are generated primarily on embryonic day (E) 11-E12 and acquire their terminal peptidergic phenotype during mid-late gestation (Padilla et al., 2010).
evidence: Supported by citation to Padilla et al., 2010.

claim: miRNAs have recently emerged as critical regulators of brain development.
source: Because miRNAs have recently emerged as critical regulators of brain development and Dicer mRNA is expressed in POMC neurons during important periods of neurogenesis and cell fate, we examined whether lack of miRNA maturation in POMC neurons causes neurodevelopmental alterations.
evidence: Based on established scientific knowledge about miRNA function in brain development.

claim: The number of Pomc mRNA-expressing cells in the ARH of Pomc-Cre; DicerloxP/loxP embryos at E13 is 1.4-fold lower than that observed in control embryos.
source: The number of Pomc mRNA-expressing cells in the ARH of Pomc-Cre; DicerloxP/loxP embryos at E13 and E15 was 1.4- and 1.2-fold lower, respectively, than that observed in control embryos (Figure 2a).
evidence: Supported by in situ hybridization data and cell counts shown in Figure 2a.

claim: The number of Pomc mRNA-expressing cells in the ARH of Pomc-Cre; DicerloxP/loxP embryos at E15 is 1.2-fold lower than that observed in control embryos.
source: The number of Pomc mRNA-expressing cells in the ARH of Pomc-Cre; DicerloxP/loxP embryos at E13 and E15 was 1.4- and 1.2-fold lower, respectively, than that observed in control embryos (Figure 2a).
evidence: Supported by in situ hybridization data and cell counts shown in Figure 2a.

claim: Pomc-Cre; DicerloxP/loxP mice at P10 display a 1.3-fold reduction in the number of Pomc mRNA-expressing cells.
source: Pomc-Cre; DicerloxP/loxP mice P10 and P14 displayed a 1.3- and 1.5-fold reduction, respectively, in the number of Pomc mRNA-expressing cells (Figure 2a; Figure 2—figure supplement 1a).
evidence: Supported by in situ hybridization data and cell counts shown in Figure 2a.

claim: Pomc-Cre; DicerloxP/loxP mice at P14 display a 1.5-fold reduction in the number of Pomc mRNA-expressing cells.
source: Pomc-Cre; DicerloxP/loxP mice P10 and P14 displayed a 1.3- and 1.5-fold reduction, respectively, in the number of Pomc mRNA-expressing cells (Figure 2a; Figure 2—figure supplement 1a).
evidence: Supported by in situ hybridization data and cell counts shown in Figure 2a and Figure 2—figure supplement 1a.

claim: At weaning (P21) there is an 8.0-fold reduction in the number of Pomc mRNA-expressing cells between mutant and control mice.
source: At weaning (P21) and in 15-week-old animals there was an 8.0- and 8.7-fold reduction, respectively, in the number of Pomc mRNA-expressing cells between mutant and control mice (Figure 2a).
evidence: Supported by in situ hybridization data and cell counts shown in Figure 2a.

claim: In 15-week-old animals there is an 8.7-fold reduction in the number of Pomc mRNA-expressing cells between mutant and control mice.
source: At weaning (P21) and in 15-week-old animals there was an 8.0- and 8.7-fold reduction, respectively, in the number of Pomc mRNA-expressing cells between mutant and control mice (Figure 2a).
evidence: Supported by in situ hybridization data and cell counts shown in Figure 2a.

claim: The marked reduction in the number of Pomc mRNA-expressing cells is accompanied by a decrease in Pomc mRNA content in the hypothalamus of P21 and 15-week-old mice.
source: This marked reduction in the number of Pomc mRNA-expressing cells was accompanied by a decrease in Pomc mRNA content in the hypothalamus of P21 and 15-week-old mice (Figure 2b).
evidence: Supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 2b.

claim: A 3.7-fold reduction in the number of β-endorphin-immunoreactive cells is found in the ARH of Pomc-Cre; DicerloxP/loxP mice.
source: In addition, a 3.7-fold reduction in the number of β-endorphin-immunoreactive cells (a peptide produced from POMC) was found in the ARH of Pomc-Cre; DicerloxP/loxP mice (Figure 2—figure supplement 1b).
evidence: Supported by immunohistochemistry data and cell counts shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1b.

claim: The density of α-MSH-immunoreactive fibers is 7.3-fold decreased in the magnocellular part of the PVH of mutant mice.
source: In addition, the density of α-MSH- and β-endorphin-immunoreactive fibers was 7.3- and 11.3-fold decreased, respectively, in the magnocellular part of the PVH and 5.7- and 10.3-fold decreased, respectively, in the parvicellular part of the PVH of mutant mice (Figure 2d).
evidence: Supported by immunohistochemistry data and fiber density measurements shown in Figure 2d.

claim: The density of β-endorphin-immunoreactive fibers is 11.3-fold decreased in the magnocellular part of the PVH of mutant mice.
source: In addition, the density of α-MSH- and β-endorphin-immunoreactive fibers was 7.3- and 11.3-fold decreased, respectively, in the magnocellular part of the PVH and 5.7- and 10.3-fold decreased, respectively, in the parvicellular part of the PVH of mutant mice (Figure 2d).
evidence: Supported by immunohistochemistry data and fiber density measurements shown in Figure 2d.

claim: The density of α-MSH-immunoreactive fibers is 5.7-fold decreased in the parvicellular part of the PVH of mutant mice.
source: In addition, the density of α-MSH- and β-endorphin-immunoreactive fibers was 7.3- and 11.3-fold decreased, respectively, in the magnocellular part of the PVH and 5.7- and 10.3-fold decreased, respectively, in the parvicellular part of the PVH of mutant mice (Figure 2d).
evidence: Supported by immunohistochemistry data and fiber density measurements shown in Figure 2d.

claim: The density of β-endorphin-immunoreactive fibers is 10.3-fold decreased in the parvicellular part of the PVH of mutant mice.
source: In addition, the density of α-MSH- and β-endorphin-immunoreactive fibers was 7.3- and 11.3-fold decreased, respectively, in the magnocellular part of the PVH and 5.7- and 10.3-fold decreased, respectively, in the parvicellular part of the PVH of mutant mice (Figure 2d).
evidence: Supported by immunohistochemistry data and fiber density measurements shown in Figure 2d.

claim: The number of tdTomato+ cells is identical between Pomc-Cre; DicerloxP/loxP and DicerloxP/loxP mice at E15.
source: Despite a marked reduction in the number of Pomc mRNA-expressing cells at E15 (Figure 2a), the number of tdTomato+ cells was identical between Pomc-Cre; DicerloxP/loxP and DicerloxP/loxP mice at E15 (Figure 2c).
evidence: Supported by cell lineage tracing data and cell counts shown in Figure 2c.

claim: At P14 there is a 1.9-fold reduction in the number of tdTomato+ cells in mutant mice.
source: At P14 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1d) and weaning (P21, Figure 2c), we observed a 1.9- and 2.9-fold reduction, respectively, in the number of tdTomato+ cells in mutant mice.
evidence: Supported by cell lineage tracing data and cell counts shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1d.

claim: At weaning (P21) there is a 2.9-fold reduction in the number of tdTomato+ cells in mutant mice.
source: At P14 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1d) and weaning (P21, Figure 2c), we observed a 1.9- and 2.9-fold reduction, respectively, in the number of tdTomato+ cells in mutant mice.
evidence: Supported by cell lineage tracing data and cell counts shown in Figure 2c.

claim: The number of tdTomato+ cells found in the ARH is 4-fold reduced at 15 weeks of age.
source: The number of tdTomato+ cells found in the ARH was 4-fold reduced at 15 weeks of age (Figure 2c) but this reduction was not as marked as the decrease in the number of Pomc mRNA-expressing cells that we observed using in situ hybridization (8.7-fold, Figure 2a).
evidence: Supported by cell lineage tracing data and cell counts shown in Figure 2c.

claim: The reduction in tdTomato+ cells at 15 weeks is not as marked as the decrease in the number of Pomc mRNA-expressing cells.
source: The number of tdTomato+ cells found in the ARH was 4-fold reduced at 15 weeks of age (Figure 2c) but this reduction was not as marked as the decrease in the number of Pomc mRNA-expressing cells that we observed using in situ hybridization (8.7-fold, Figure 2a).
evidence: Comparison of data from Figure 2c and Figure 2a.

claim: The reduction in POMC cell numbers is caused by a decrease in Pomc detectability versus cell loss.
source: These observations indicate that this reduction in POMC cell numbers is caused by a decrease in Pomc detectability versus cell loss.
evidence: Inferred from the discrepancy between tdTomato+ cell counts and Pomc mRNA-expressing cell counts.

claim: A significant reduction in POMC-immunoreactive cell numbers is observed in the pituitary of mutant mice.
source: In addition, a significant reduction in POMC-immunoreactive cell numbers was observed in the pituitary of mutant mice but no change in tdTomato +cell numbers was found in the NTS, another brain site that contains POMC neurons (Figure 2—figure supplement 1e and f).
evidence: Supported by immunohistochemistry data and cell counts shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1e.

claim: No change in tdTomato+ cell numbers is found in the NTS of mutant mice.
source: In addition, a significant reduction in POMC-immunoreactive cell numbers was observed in the pituitary of mutant mice but no change in tdTomato +cell numbers was found in the NTS, another brain site that contains POMC neurons (Figure 2—figure supplement 1e and f).
evidence: Supported by cell lineage tracing data and cell counts shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1f.

claim: Loss of Dicer in hypothalamic Pomc progenitor cells causes postnatal cell death.
source: These observations support the idea that loss of Dicer in hypothalamic Pomc progenitor cells causes postnatal cell death but also blunts Pomc gene expression and might favor acquisition of a non-POMC phenotype.
evidence: Inferred from the reduction in tdTomato+ cells over time.

claim: Loss of Dicer in hypothalamic Pomc progenitor cells blunts Pomc gene expression.
source: These observations support the idea that loss of Dicer in hypothalamic Pomc progenitor cells causes postnatal cell death but also blunts Pomc gene expression and might favor acquisition of a non-POMC phenotype.
evidence: Inferred from the discrepancy between tdTomato+ cells and Pomc mRNA-expressing cells.

claim: Loss of Dicer in hypothalamic Pomc progenitor cells might favor acquisition of a non-POMC phenotype.
source: These observations support the idea that loss of Dicer in hypothalamic Pomc progenitor cells causes postnatal cell death but also blunts Pomc gene expression and might favor acquisition of a non-POMC phenotype.
evidence: Speculative inference based on the observation that some tdTomato+ cells do not express Pomc mRNA.

claim: Pomc progenitors are known to adopt a POMC but also a non-POMC phenotype such as NPY.
source: Because Pomc progenitors are known to adopt a POMC but also a non-POMC phenotype such as NPY (Padilla et al., 2010), we next quantified the number of NPY neurons in the ARH of control and mutant mice.
evidence: Supported by citation to Padilla et al., 2010.

claim: The number of Npy mRNA-expressing neurons is identical between Pomc-Cre; DicerloxP/loxP and DicerloxP/loxP mice at E15, P14, and P21.
source: First we performed in situ hybridizations and counted the number of Npy mRNA-expressing neurons and found that it was identical between Pomc-Cre; DicerloxP/loxP and DicerloxP/loxP mice at E15, P14, and P21 (Figure 3a; Figure 2—figure supplement 1c).
evidence: Supported by in situ hybridization data and cell counts shown in Figure 3a and Figure 2—figure supplement 1c.

claim: Npy mRNA levels in the hypothalamus are comparable between Pomc-Cre; DicerloxP/loxP and DicerloxP/loxP mice.
source: Consistent with these findings, RT-qPCR experiments indicated that Npy mRNA levels in the hypothalamus were comparable between Pomc-Cre; DicerloxP/loxP and DicerloxP/loxP mice (Figure 3b).
evidence: Supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 3b.

claim: There is no difference in the density of NPY-immunoreactive fibers between control and mutant mice at P21.
source: We also performed immunohistochemical analyses and found no difference in the density of NPY-immunoreactive fibers between control and mutant mice at P21 (Figure 3d).
evidence: Supported by immunohistochemistry data and fiber density measurements shown in Figure 3d.

claim: Lack of Dicer does not cause death of Pomc progenitors that subsequently adopt a NPY phenotype.
source: Together, these results support the hypothesis that lack of Dicer does not cause death of Pomc progenitors that subsequently adopt a NPY phenotype.
evidence: Inferred from the observation that NPY neuron numbers are unchanged in mutant mice.

claim: At birth (P0) the proportion of Pomc-expressing progenitor cells that became NPY neurons is 1.6-fold increased in mutant compared to control mice.
source: At birth (P0) and P21, the proportion of Pomc-expressing progenitor cells that became NPY neurons was 1.6- and 1.3-fold increased, respectively, in mutant compared to control mice (Figure 3c).
evidence: Supported by cell lineage tracing data and cell counts shown in Figure 3c.

claim: At P21 the proportion of Pomc-expressing progenitor cells that became NPY neurons is 1.3-fold increased in mutant compared to control mice.
source: At birth (P0) and P21, the proportion of Pomc-expressing progenitor cells that became NPY neurons was 1.6- and 1.3-fold increased, respectively, in mutant compared to control mice (Figure 3c).
evidence: Supported by cell lineage tracing data and cell counts shown in Figure 3c.

claim: Loss of miRNA maturation in POMC neurons favors the differentiation of Pomc progenitor cells into mature NPY neurons.
source: These data indicate that loss of miRNA maturation in POMC neurons favors the differentiation of Pomc progenitor cells into mature NPY neurons.
evidence: Inferred from the increased proportion of Pomc progenitors becoming NPY neurons in mutant mice.

claim: E15 represents an important developmental period for the differentiation of Pomc progenitor cells into either a POMC or a NPY phenotype.
source: We specifically studied embryos at E15 because this age represents an important developmental period for the differentiation of Pomc progenitor cells into either a POMC or a NPY phenotype (Padilla et al., 2010).
evidence: Supported by citation to Padilla et al., 2010.

claim: GFP-positive cells sorted from Pomc-eGFP hypothalami contain high levels of Pomc mRNA and low levels of Npy mRNA.
source: As expected, GFP-positive cells sorted from Pomc-eGFP hypothalami contained high levels of Pomc mRNA and low levels of Npy mRNA (Figure 4c and d).
evidence: Supported by RT-qPCR data from sorted cells shown in Figure 4c and d.

claim: GFP-positive cells sorted from Npy-hrGFP hypothalami contain high levels of Npy mRNA and very low levels of Pomc mRNA.
source: In contrast, GFP-positive cells sorted from Npy-hrGFP hypothalami and GFP +tdTomato cells sorted from Pomc-Cre; tdTomato; Npy-hrGFP embryos contained high levels of Npy mRNA and very low levels of Pomc mRNA (Figure 4c and d; Figure 4—figure supplement 1a).
evidence: Supported by RT-qPCR data from sorted cells shown in Figure 4c and d.

claim: GFP+tdTomato cells sorted from Pomc-Cre; tdTomato; Npy-hrGFP embryos contain high levels of Npy mRNA and very low levels of Pomc mRNA.
source: In contrast, GFP-positive cells sorted from Npy-hrGFP hypothalami and GFP +tdTomato cells sorted from Pomc-Cre; tdTomato; Npy-hrGFP embryos contained high levels of Npy mRNA and very low levels of Pomc mRNA (Figure 4c and d; Figure 4—figure supplement 1a).
evidence: Supported by RT-qPCR data from sorted cells shown in Figure 4c, d, and Figure 4—figure supplement 1a.

claim: Out of 722 miRNA-specific probe sets, expression of 46 miRNAs is significantly changed in E15 Pomc→NPY cells compared with E15 Pomc→POMC cells.
source: Out of 722 miRNA-specific probe sets, expression of 46 miRNAs was significantly changed in E15 Pomc→NPY cells compared with E15 Pomc→POMC cells, of which 22% were increased and 78% were decreased (Figure 4e and f; Figure 4—figure supplement 1b; Supplementary file 1).
evidence: Supported by miRNA microarray data shown in Figure 4e, f, and Figure 4—figure supplement 1b.

claim: 22% of the 46 differentially expressed miRNAs were increased in E15 Pomc→NPY cells compared with E15 Pomc→POMC cells.
source: Out of 722 miRNA-specific probe sets, expression of 46 miRNAs was significantly changed in E15 Pomc→NPY cells compared with E15 Pomc→POMC cells, of which 22% were increased and 78% were decreased (Figure 4e and f; Figure 4—figure supplement 1b; Supplementary file 1).
evidence: Supported by miRNA microarray data shown in Figure 4e, f, and Figure 4—figure supplement 1b.

claim: 78% of the 46 differentially expressed miRNAs were decreased in E15 Pomc→NPY cells compared with E15 Pomc→POMC cells.
source: Out of 722 miRNA-specific probe sets, expression of 46 miRNAs was significantly changed in E15 Pomc→NPY cells compared with E15 Pomc→POMC cells, of which 22% were increased and 78% were decreased (Figure 4e and f; Figure 4—figure supplement 1b; Supplementary file 1).
evidence: Supported by miRNA microarray data shown in Figure 4e, f, and Figure 4—figure supplement 1b.

claim: The miRNA screen revealed a marked reduction in the expression of miR-103 and miR-107.
source: Particularly, this screen revealed a marked reduction in the expression of miR-103 and miR-107, two miRNAs that have been previously associated with obesity-induced insulin resistance in the liver and adipose tissue (Trajkovski et al., 2011).
evidence: Supported by miRNA microarray data.

claim: miR-103 and miR-107 have been previously associated with obesity-induced insulin resistance in the liver and adipose tissue.
source: Particularly, this screen revealed a marked reduction in the expression of miR-103 and miR-107, two miRNAs that have been previously associated with obesity-induced insulin resistance in the liver and adipose tissue (Trajkovski et al., 2011).
evidence: Supported by citation to Trajkovski et al., 2011.

claim: miR-103 levels are 4.0-fold down-regulated in E15 Pomc→NPY cells compared with E15 Pomc→POMC cells.
source: Using RT-qPCR, we confirmed that miR-103 and miR-107 levels were 4.0- to 4.5-fold down-regulated in E15 Pomc→NPY cells compared with E15 Pomc→POMC cells (Figure 4g).
evidence: Supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 4g.

claim: miR-107 levels are 4.5-fold down-regulated in E15 Pomc→NPY cells compared with E15 Pomc→POMC cells.
source: Using RT-qPCR, we confirmed that miR-103 and miR-107 levels were 4.0- to 4.5-fold down-regulated in E15 Pomc→NPY cells compared with E15 Pomc→POMC cells (Figure 4g).
evidence: Supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 4g.

claim: A 3.2-fold reduction in miR-103 expression is observed in sorted Pomc cells of Pomc-Cre; DicerloxP/loxP mice.
source: Moreover, a 3.2- and 1.4-fold reduction in miR-103 and miR-107 expression, respectively, was observed in sorted Pomc cells of Pomc-Cre; DicerloxP/loxP mice (Figure 4—figure supplement 1c).
evidence: Supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1c.

claim: A 1.4-fold reduction in miR-107 expression is observed in sorted Pomc cells of Pomc-Cre; DicerloxP/loxP mice.
source: Moreover, a 3.2- and 1.4-fold reduction in miR-103 and miR-107 expression, respectively, was observed in sorted Pomc cells of Pomc-Cre; DicerloxP/loxP mice (Figure 4—figure supplement 1c).
evidence: Supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1c.

claim: miR-103/107 might play a key role in determining whether a Pomc progenitor acquires a POMC or a NPY phenotype.
source: These data indicate that miR-103/107 might play a key role in determining whether a Pomc progenitor acquires a POMC or a NPY phenotype.
evidence: Inferred from the differential expression of miR-103/107 in Pomc→POMC versus Pomc→NPY cells.

claim: Ant-107 causes a 2.2-fold decrease in miR-107 expression 72 hr post-injection.
source: RT-qPCR analysis 72 hr post-injection revealed that Ant-107 caused a 2.2-fold decrease in miR-107 expression (Figure 4h).
evidence: Supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 4h.

claim: Ant-107 also down-regulates miR-103 expression.
source: As previously reported (Trajkovski et al., 2011), Ant-107 also down-regulated miR-103 expression (data not shown).
evidence: Supported by citation to Trajkovski et al., 2011 and unpublished data.

claim: No correlation is observed between Pomc mRNA and miR-107 expression.
source: No correlation was observed between Pomc mRNA and miR-107 expression (Figure 4i).
evidence: Supported by correlation analysis shown in Figure 4i.

claim: In embryos with greater than 60% knockdown efficiency, blocking miR-107 causes a 2.4-fold decrease in Pomc mRNA expression.
source: However, in embryos that displayed a knockdown efficiency greater than 60%, we found that blocking miR-107 caused a 2.4-fold decrease in Pomc mRNA expression (Figure 4j).
evidence: Supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 4j.

claim: There is a negative correlation between Npy mRNA expression and miR-107 expression.
source: In addition, there was a negative correlation between Npy mRNA expression and miR-107 expression (Figure 4k).
evidence: Supported by correlation analysis shown in Figure 4k.

claim: When embryos display a knockdown efficiency greater than 60%, there is a 3.9-fold increase in Npy mRNA expression compared to control.
source: When embryos displayed a knockdown efficiency greater than 60%, there was a 3.9-fold increase in Npy mRNA expression compared to control (Figure 4l).
evidence: Supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 4l.

claim: The addition of Ant-107 to the culture medium produces a 4.9-fold reduction in miR-107 expression after 72 hr.
source: After 72 hr, the addition of the Ant-107 to the culture medium produced a 4.9-fold reduction in miR-107 expression (Figure 4m).
evidence: Supported by RT-qPCR data from organotypic explants shown in Figure 4m.

claim: The reduction in miR-107 expression is accompanied with a 3.2-fold increase in the proportion of Pomc progenitors that differentiate into NPY neurons.
source: This reduction in miR-107 expression was accompanied with a 3.2-fold increase in the proportion of Pomc progenitors that differentiate into NPY neurons (Figure 4n).
evidence: Supported by cell lineage tracing data from organotypic explants shown in Figure 4n.

claim: The silencing of miR-107 is accompanied with a 1.2-fold reduction in the number of Pomc-expressing progenitors that express Pomc-eGFP.
source: Interestingly, the silencing of miR-107 is also accompanied with a 1.2-fold reduction in the number of Pomc-expressing progenitors that express Pomc-eGFP (Figure 4o).
evidence: Supported by cell counts from organotypic explants shown in Figure 4o.

claim: A reduction in miR-107 expression favors the differentiation of Pomc progenitors into a NPY phenotype versus a POMC phenotype.
source: These observations support the hypothesis that a reduction in miR-107 expression favors the differentiation of Pomc progenitors into a NPY phenotype versus a POMC phenotype.
evidence: Inferred from the in vitro experiments showing increased NPY differentiation with miR-107 inhibition.

claim: A 2-fold reduction in miR-107 expression is observed in the hypothalami of E14 embryos that received LNA-107 at E12 compared to control mice.

evidence: Supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 4p and Figure 4—figure supplement 1d.

claim: The pre- and post-weaning growth curves (body weights) of mice injected with LNA-107 prenatally are indistinguishable from those of control mice.
source: Physiologically, the pre- and post-weaning growth curves (body weights) of injected mice injected with LNA-107 prenatally were undistinguishable from those of control mice (Figure 4q).

claim: Body composition is similar between LNA-107-injected and control mice.
source: Similarly, body composition was similar between LNA-107-injected and control mice (Figure 4r).

claim: Adult mice that received LNA-107 injections prenatally and had 34% loss in POMC neurons display impaired glucose tolerance compared with control mice.
source: However, when exposed to a glucose challenge, adult mice that received LNA-107 injections prenatally and had 34% loss in POMC neurons displayed impaired glucose tolerance compared with control mice (Figure 4s).
evidence: Supported by glucose tolerance test data shown in Figure 4s.

claim: There is a negative correlation between the glucose area under the curve during GTT and the number of POMC neurons.
source: In addition, there was a negative correlation between the glucose area under the curve during GTT and the number of POMC neurons (Figure 4t).

claim: Small non-coding RNAs or miRNAs are involved in the regulation of metabolism and neural development.
source: Several lines of evidence have indicated that small non-coding RNAs or miRNAs are involved in the regulation of metabolism and neural development (Coolen and Bally-Cuif, 2009; Oliverio et al., 2016; Fineberg et al., 2009; Vo et al., 2010; Deiuliis, 2016; McGregor and Choi, 2011; Schneeberger et al., 2012; Jordan et al., 2011; Kornfeld et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to previous studies.

claim: Loss of Dicer in POMC neurons causes metabolic disturbances in mice associated with an age-related decline in the number of Pomc mRNA-expressing cells.
source: In the present study, we report that loss of Dicer, an enzyme critical to process miRNA precursors (pre-miRNAs) into mature miRNAs (miRNAs), in POMC neurons causes metabolic disturbances in mice associated with an age-related decline in the number of Pomc mRNA-expressing cells.
evidence: Summary of findings from the study combining metabolic and neuroanatomical data.

claim: Dicer influences the peptidergic differentiation of Pomc progenitor cells during embryonic life.
source: We also show that Dicer influences the peptidergic differentiation of Pomc progenitor cells during embryonic life, a developmental process that appears to be specifically mediated through miR-103/107.
evidence: Summary of findings from cell lineage tracing experiments.

claim: The peptidergic differentiation of Pomc progenitor cells appears to be specifically mediated through miR-103/107.
source: We also show that Dicer influences the peptidergic differentiation of Pomc progenitor cells during embryonic life, a developmental process that appears to be specifically mediated through miR-103/107.

claim: The majority of neurons located in the mouse hypothalamus, including POMC neurons, are born between E11 and E12.

evidence: Speculative inference based on early reduction in POMC cell numbers and comparison to other brain regions.

claim: The distribution pattern of POMC neurons in mutant mice resembles that of control mice.

claim: Dicer does not influence POMC cell migration.
source: The distribution pattern of POMC neurons in mutant mice resembles that of control mice, supporting the idea that Dicer does not influence POMC cell migration.
evidence: Inferred from the observation that POMC neuron distribution is similar between mutant and control mice.

claim: Dicer deficiency causes a marked reduction in the number of Pomc mRNA-expressing cells particularly after birth.
source: Our neuroanatomical analysis also revealed that Dicer deficiency causes a marked reduction in the number of Pomc mRNA-expressing cells particularly after birth and that 90% of POMC+ cells are loss in the arcuate nucleus of adult Pomc-Cre; DicerloxP/loxP mice.
evidence: Inferred from the temporal pattern of POMC cell loss shown in the data.

claim: 90% of POMC+ cells are lost in the arcuate nucleus of adult Pomc-Cre; DicerloxP/loxP mice.
source: Our neuroanatomical analysis also revealed that Dicer deficiency causes a marked reduction in the number of Pomc mRNA-expressing cells particularly after birth and that 90% of POMC+ cells are loss in the arcuate nucleus of adult Pomc-Cre; DicerloxP/loxP mice.
evidence: Calculated from the 8.7-fold reduction in POMC cells at 15 weeks.

claim: The dramatic reduction in the number of Pomc mRNA-expressing neurons might be the result of increased cell death.
source: This dramatic reduction in the number of Pomc mRNA-expressing neurons might be the result of increased cell death consistent with previous papers implicating Dicer and miRNAs in cell survival of various neuronal systems including the retina, the neural crest, and the hypothalamus (Sundermeier et al., 2014; Zehir et al., 2010; Damiani et al., 2008; Schneeberger et al., 2012).
evidence: Speculative inference based on comparison to other neuronal systems and supported by citations.

claim: A significant number of neurons survive in mutant mice and Pomc mRNA expression is blunted in these neurons.
source: However, our cell lineage tracing experiments that allowed us to genetically label Pomc-expressing cells, independently of Pomc mRNA content, further revealed that a significant number of neurons survive in mutant mice and that Pomc mRNA expression is blunted in these neurons.
evidence: Inferred from the discrepancy between tdTomato+ cells and Pomc mRNA-expressing cells.

claim: Future studies using temporal deletion of Dicer are required to investigate its relative contribution on developmental processes versus adult regulations.
source: Because in our mouse model Cre activity is turned on in Pomc-expressing cells from embryonic life to adulthood, future studies using temporal deletion of Dicer are required to investigate its relative contribution on developmental processes versus adult regulations.
evidence: Acknowledgment of study limitation and suggestion for future research.

When progenitors differentiate in mature neurons, REST leaves the miR-124a loci enabling miR-124a to repress non-neuronal transcripts (Conaco et al., 2006).
